title: 2011 HMMT February Team Round 2 Problem 10
statement: Let the circumcircle of triangle \(A O M\) intersect \(\omega\) again at \(D\). Prove that points \(A, D\), and \(X\) are collinear.

solutions.text: By the similarity \(\triangle O A M \sim O X A\), we have that \(\angle O A X=\angle O M A\). Since \(A O M D\) is a cyclic quadrilateral, we have that \(\angle O M A=\angle O D A\). Since \(O A=O D\), we have that \(\angle O D A=\angle O A D\). Combining these equations tells us that \(\angle O A X=\angle O A D\), so \(A, D\), and \(X\) are collinear, as desired.
